Beta blockers are usually continued perioperatively although the anaesthetist must be informed of their use (see Precautions, above). However, the hypotensive ef- fects of beta blockers may be potentiated by general anaesthetics, and anaesthetics that cause myocardial depression, such as ether, cyclopropane, and trichloroethylene should preferably be avoid- ed. Histamine H2-antagonists. Plasma concentrations of pro- pranolol and metoprolol may be increased by cimetidine;1 phar- macokinetic studies indicate that cimetidine exerts its effect by reducing hepatic blood flow and impairing beta blocker metabo- lism. Cimetidine has been reported to increase the bioavailability of labetalol,1 and to increase the systemic effects of timolol eye drops.2 1. Smith SR, Kendall MJ.
